packages.label: שַׁבָּת וְהַצַּדִּיק — אוֹר הָעֵינַיִם
packages.label_en: Shabbat and the Tzaddik — Light of the Eyes
packages.reason: All these nodes share the essential nature of divine illumination as channeled through the Tzaddik and through Shabbat. The core teaching equates the Tzaddik with Shabbat (both are 'Shem d'Kudsha Berikh Hu'), and both produce the three colors of the eye (תלת גונין דעינא ובת עין), which are the light of the eyes (מאור העינים), which is the light of the Temple (the Temple = עינים), which is the beauty and splendor of the Tzaddik (פאר), which is the intellect/mohin (מחין). All the structural equivalents — the house (בית), the tefillin-boxes (בתים של התפלין), the Tzaddik as primordial foundation (יסוד הפשוט), the four elements flowing from him, the holy name (שם ה / שם הקדש), and Noah as prototype of the departed Tzaddik — are all expressions of the same essential reality: the illumination that the true Tzaddik-head brings into the world, opening eyes and sustaining the Temple. The good/evil mirror: this entire package mirrors Package 2 (false heads, fire-lights) and Package 3 (the evil fire that burns when this light departs).

merge_notes.reason: These five nodes form a structural cluster around the Temple/House. The Torah explicitly equates בית המקדש with עינים (eyes); the בתים של התפלין are where the מחין dwell; the דירה is the dwelling-place produced by Shabbat. All are expressions of the same essential reality as the illuminated house that the Tzaddik-head sustains — same shared nature as the main cluster, not a causal relationship. Bechina: the house IS the eyes, the eyes IS the Temple.

These three are all bechina-expressions of the Tzaddik as the primordial simple foundation from which all four elements flow. The Torah says: 'נהר יוצא מעדן — זה בחינת צדיק יסוד עולם, שהוא בחינת יסוד הפשוט.' They share the same essential nature as the צדיק האמת / ראש בית nodes in the main cluster — all are facets of the Tzaddik's foundational role. Merged because they are bechina (same nature) with the Tzaddik-cluster, not eitza to it.

The Torah explicitly states: 'הבכיה הוא בחינת הסתלקות מאורי אור' — crying IS the withdrawal of the lights of illumination. These are two aspects of the same reality. Thematically, this pair describes the *absence* of holy light (the negative face of the מאורי אור / תלת גונין cluster). Bechina: crying and light-withdrawal are not cause-and-effect but two expressions of the same inner reality of exile and concealment.

West = setting of light. The Torah states: 'וזה בחינת שקיעת האור במערב' — the west IS the setting of light. These are two facets of the same geographic-spiritual reality. The West is the direction where the Shechina weeps (= מאור העינים departs), connecting this pair to the central eye-light theme of Package 1. Bechina: the west shares the same essential nature as the setting of divine light.

The Torah states: 'מסתלק מאור עינים — זה בחינת שקיעת האור במערב' — the withdrawal of the eye-light IS the setting of light in the west. These are two descriptions of the same withdrawal phenomenon, belonging to the same holy-light cluster as the absence-thereof.

When the Tzaddik (ראש בית) is present, the entire generation are 'children of the house.' The Torah states: 'כולנו, דהיינו כל בני הדור, כולם בחינת בני בית.' These two nodes are bechina-equivalent: all of the generation share the same essential nature as members of the Tzaddik-household. Merged into Package 1 since the concept only makes sense within the ראש בית / holy-Tzaddik reality.

The Torah identifies Shem (שם, Noah's son) as שם הקדש = פאר והדור = the primary adornment. The holy name and the adornment-splendor are bechina-equivalent. These belong to the main cluster's שם ה / פאר / Tzaddik-name sub-theme: the same essential reality of the divine name embodied in the Tzaddik's fame.

The Torah equates: 'ומשם יפרד והיה לארבעה ראשים — הינו בחינת הארבעה יסודות, שנמשכין מן הצדיק.' The scriptural phrase IS the four elements — both are expressions of the same structural reality of how multiplicity flows from the Tzaddik-unity. Bechina: the verse-phrase and the concept share the same nature. Merged into Package 1 as part of the Tzaddik-as-foundation sub-cluster.

packages.label: מְאוֹרֵי הָאֵשׁ וְהַחֻרְבָּן
packages.reason: These three nodes all share the essential nature of destructive fire-energy that is the direct opposite of the holy light (מאורי אור). The Torah states: 'יש מאורי אור ומאורי אש והם זה לעומת זה.' The ash (אפר) IS the fire-lights in their aftermath-form; the fire-lights ARE the burning of the Temple. They are three faces of the same destructive cosmic force that erupts when holy illumination withdraws. The Torah explicitly equates אפר with מאורי אש ('אפר — זה בחינת מאורי אש') and מאורי אש with שרפת בית המקדש. Good/evil mirror: this package is the exact negative mirror of the מאורי אור cluster in Package 1.

packages.label: רֹאשׁ הַסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא — הַמְפֻרְסָמִים שֶׁל שֶׁקֶר
packages.label_en: Head of the Other Side — the False Famous Ones
packages.reason: These three nodes are all expressions of the evil counterfeit of the holy Tzaddik-head (ראש בית). The Torah states: 'ראש של הסטרא אחרא — בחינת מפרסמים של שקר, בחינת שמות הטומאה של החיצונים.' They are three aspects of the same evil reality: the false famous ones who propagate the impure names of the sitra achra in place of God's name. Their essential nature is counterfeit leadership and impure naming. Good/evil mirror: this package directly mirrors Package 1's ראש בית / שם ה sub-cluster — same structure of 'a head whose name fills the world,' but aligned with evil.
